items.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
items.summary: Last year, Trump accused South Africa of white genocide in a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House US President Donald Trump has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme, from 1 January 2027 The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the US duty-free US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements He added that the Trump administration had additionally notified the two countries of the decision The Trump administration cited barriers to US trade and investment, as well as concerns over national security and foreign policy interests in the region For South Africa, the US pointed to corruption In a letter to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Trump said Pretoria's actions on international security and its relations and cooperation with governments of concern to Washington risked…

items.title: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
items.summary: More than 50 people are feared to be trapped under the rubble Russian strikes on Ukraine – including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital – have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others over the last 24 hours At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war" Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly…

items.title: Greenland's parliament ratifies Trump's US security agreement
items.summary: The US is set to expand its military footprint on the Arctic island, part of the Kingdom of Denmark. It follows pressure from Donald Trump earlier in the year which opened a major rift in the transatlantic alliance Greenland's parliament on Tuesday signed off on a trilateral security and military-access agreement with the United States and Denmark that paves the way for an expanded US' military presence on the strategically located and mineral-rich island The deal has alleviated pressure coming from US President Donald Trump , who earlier this year had repeatedly threatened to take control of the self-governing Danish territory, citing US security interests After months of negotiation the agreement was signed in September by Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York The agreement allows for two new US military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system.

items.title: UK's King Charles III decries 'monstrous injustice' of slave trade
items.summary: King Charles has told leaders at a Commonwealth summit that the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade "fills my heart with horror." He did not address calls for apologies and reparations The United Kingdom 's King Charles III on Tuesday opened this week's Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda , a summit of 56 Commonwealth member-state leaders, by speaking of the tragic legacy of the transatlantic slave trade Charles told those gathered that he had furthered his "own understanding of the issues through listening, learning and looking." "The ​transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth. As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with ⁠horror ​and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow." The monarch stopped short of apologizing for Britain's role in the dark trade, as well as refraining from any talk of reparations .

items.title: Uganda arrests former army deputy chief stripped of military rank
items.summary: Uganda accuses Peter Elwelu of stockpiling weapons and organising activities against the government Uganda has arrested former deputy military chief and presidential adviser Peter Elwelu over allegations of involvement in activities aimed at destabilising the country Acting military spokesman Chris Magezi said Elwelu, whom he described as a "renegade" officer, was arrested on Monday evening and would be charged in court The arrest comes days after Uganda's defence chief, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, announced that he had stripped Elwelu of his lieutenant general rank and demoted him to a private Elwelu has not commented on the allegations Elwelu rose to prominence in 2016 when he oversaw a deadly military raid on the palace of a regional king accused of leading a separatist movement. He was subsequently appointed army chief He later rose to become the deputy chief of defence forces before being named presidential adviser In May 2024, the US government imposed sanctions on him over alleged human rights abuses, including extrajudicial killings committed by government forces.
